questions.question_text: What is the primary goal of clarity and articulation in verbal communication, as discussed in the chapter?

options.text: To speak as quickly as possible to keep the audience engaged
To ensure words are easy to understand and pronounced distinctly
To use complex vocabulary to impress listeners
To avoid speaking in front of large audiencesCorrect Answer:B. To ensure words are easy to understand and pronounced distinctly

questions.question_text: According to the chapter, how can tone impact the delivery of a message?

options.text: It has no effect on how the audience perceives the message
It conveys emotion and intent, influencing how listeners feel about what is said
It only matters in formal speeches, not casual conversations
It should always remain neutral to avoid confusionCorrect Answer:B. It conveys emotion and intent, influencing how listeners feel about what is said

questions.question_text: What is one benefit of using emphasis in speech, as highlighted in the chapter?

options.text: It makes the speaker sound louder regardless of content
It helps highlight important words or ideas to grab audience attention
It slows down the speech to fill more time
It prevents the need for preparation before speakingCorrect Answer:B. It helps highlight important words or ideas to grab audience attention

questions.question_text: How does the chapter suggest using pauses effectively in a speech?

options.text: To fill time when the speaker forgets what to say next
To build drama, emphasize points, and give the audience time to think
To avoid making eye contact with the audience
To speak faster and finish the speech soonerCorrect Answer:B. To build drama, emphasize points, and give the audience time to think

questions.question_text: What is a common reason teens use filler words like “um” or “like,” according to the chapter?

options.text: They are always intentional and add meaning to speech
They occur when nervous, buying time to think, or out of habit
They are necessary to keep the audience’s attention
They make the speaker sound more professionalCorrect Answer:B. They occur when nervous, buying time to think, or out of habit

questions.question_text: What is one strategy the chapter recommends for reducing filler words in speech?

options.text: Speaking as fast as possible to avoid hesitation
Replacing fillers with silent pauses or purposeful phrases like “Let me think”
Ignoring fillers since they don’t affect communication
Using more complex words to distract from fillersCorrect Answer:B. Replacing fillers with silent pauses or purposeful phrases like “Let me think”
